messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Streaming latency SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (p95 0.9s -> 1.7s, p99 1.2s -> 3.2s). Impacting ~4% of live sessions. Paging @eng-oncall. thread started.
Sam: got it, i'm on call. starting triage. any customer reports yet?
Jin (CS): a couple customers (acct-A, acct-C) opened chats complaining about slow streaming and partial outputs. I'll start a heads-up.
Sam: first quick checks: metrics dashboard shows a sharp tail spike starting 2164999800 -> sustained for ~2m. Streaming proxy error rate up (502/504 spikes) and many connections in WRITE_WAIT.
Sam: pulling logs from streaming-proxy (k8s streaming-proxy/):
```
streaming-proxy-2  | 2026-06-18T12:00:05Z W write_timeout socket fd=45: client_write slow
streaming-proxy-2  | 2026-06-18T12:00:06Z E upstream: upstream write fail: broken pipe
ingress-nginx-1     | 2026-06-18T12:00:06Z 499 "GET /v1/stream?model=r1 HTTP/1.1" 0 0 "-" "curl/7.82" 0.003
```
Sam: noticing a lot of 499 from ingress which suggests slow consumers/backpressure, plus proxy is hitting socket write stalls. p99 token latency correlates with write stalls.
Maya: do we also see KV cache pressure on the runtime? that can amplify tail.
Sam: runtime KV cache hitrate is steady; no spike. this feels network/proxy-layerish or a streaming chunk flush problem.
Raj: fwiw there was a recent kernel-selection tweak rolled out 2h ago that changes socket write coalescing on some instances. could be related.
Sam: ok escalation: Raj as infra oncall, can you look at the streaming-proxy pod and ingress buffering?
Raj: on it. quick mitigation ideas: 1) disable nginx buffer for this route (X-Accel-Buffering: no), 2) increase streaming-proxy replicas from 4->8, 3) temporary fallback to non-streaming endpoint for heavy customers.
Ellie: i'll prepare a short message to affected customers & set expectation: "we're investigating; possible short-term errors/slow streaming; we will update in 30m."
Sam: executing quick checks to flip buffering header at edge for /v1/stream. if we add header X-Accel-Buffering: no at the route level it should avoid NGINX buffering and reduce write stalls for slow consumers.
Sam: applying ingress patch now:
```
kubectl patch ingress streaming-ingress -n prod --patch '{"spec":{"rules":[{"http":{"paths":[{"path":"/v1/stream","backend":{"serviceName":"streaming-proxy","servicePort":443},"pathType":"ImplementationSpecific","backendConfig":{"headers":{"X-Accel-Buffering":"no"}}}]}}]}}'
```
Raj: hold — our ingress provider doesn't accept that backendConfig shape. quick alternative: set annotation on the ingress-controller ConfigMap default-streaming-buffering = "off" for that host. I'm patching controller config.
Raj: scaled streaming-proxy deployment replicas from 4 -> 8: `kubectl scale deploy streaming-proxy -n prod --replicas=8`. watching CPU/conn.
deploy-bot: canary rollback triggered: streaming-runtime -> revert commit f3a9b2 -> previous stable f3a9b1 (affects kernel selection). rolling back 2 pods now.
Sam: good. also toggling our streaming batching: disabling prefix batching for /v1/stream to reduce large in-flight messages which may be amplifying backpressure.
Maya: i'm taking active status and will own the rest of the response; Sam handoff in 2.
Sam: handing oncall to Maya — handing over current actions: ingress buffer toggle attempted, replicas scaled, runtime rollback canary started, customer comm draft in progress.
Maya: acknowledged. Raj, any change in metrics?
Raj: after scaling and controller config update ingress buffering effectively off for the host; write stalls dropped immediately on ~60% of pods; p99 fell from 3.2s -> ~1.1s within 45s. runtime canary rollback shows improvement on canary nodes; rolling forward the rollback to all if stable for next 5m.
Maya: good. Ellie's customer message ready?
Ellie: posted to accounts A/C/D and updated status page with short blurb. linking to thread.
Ellie: message: "We've observed intermittent slow streaming and partial outputs for some customers. We've identified proxy-side write stalls and applied mitigations. Temporary fixes implemented, performance trending back to normal. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline."
Maya: next steps for mitigation until we have an RCA: 1) keep ingress buffering off for streaming host for 30m, 2) keep streaming-proxy scaled to 8 replicas, 3) roll back runtime kernel change fully if canary remains good, 4) monitor p95/p99 for 15m windows and CS alerts.
Sam: note for postmortem: include network socket write backpressure metrics (tcp retransmits, socket queues), ingress buffering config, and the kernel-selection change diff. Also check if our streaming chunk flush logic interacts badly with slow clients (e.g., no-flush until prefix reaches threshold).
Raj: telemetry note: add a short-run analytic for count of connections in WRITE_WAIT and ingress 499s per minute; we'll capture last 2h of logs and upload to incident artifact.
Maya: status update for the channel: major impact reduced, p99 trending to 0.9s. still monitoring.
incidents-bot: NOTICE: oncall handover recorded: Sam -> Maya at 2165000090.
Maya: closing timeline notes: resolved state will be set when p99 < 1.0s for 10m and error rate normalizes. assigning postmortem owners: Raj (infra), Sam (runtime), Ellie (customer comms).
Jin (CS): thanks — keeping customers updated. I'll follow up with account notes.
Maya: final: p99 has stabilized at 0.85s, error rate normalized. marked INVESTIGATING -> RESOLVED. will open postmortem ticket with timeline, root cause hypothesis (kernel-selection write coalescing + ingress buffering exposing slow-consumer write stalls) and mitigation actions (rework kernel selection, adjust default streaming buffer, add early-flush for streaming chunks).
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — duration 6m. follow-up: create postmortem in #postmortems and tag owners. :white_check_mark:
